subject: Order Form: output ownership & training consent — path forward
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightworks.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: BrightWorks Legal <legal@brightworks.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: BrightWorks redlines: order form + IP rider (output & training)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are BrightWorks' latest redlines to the order form and the IP rider. High level:

- Output ownership: we need a clear assignment for outputs that are derived from our confidential inputs when those outputs are used to create a product feature (we're asking for explicit assignment for outputs that become part of a BrightWorks product or product dataset).
- Training & feedback license: BrightWorks cannot consent to a broad training license for our customer data; we can consider a scoped feedback license (read-only telemetry and aggregated non-identifiable usage metrics) but not model retraining or fine-tuning unless separately contracted.
- Feedback/Telemetry: request an opt-in flow and the right to audit telemetry summary reports quarterly.

I've attached a redline and a short memo explaining our asks. Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept the assignment carveout (first bullet) and the scoped feedback license (second bullet)? If not, please propose alternative language we can review.

We'd like to get to a final order form by end of week. If it's easier, happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales | Sr. Counsel, BrightWorks
Attachments: BrightWorks_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx, BrightWorks_IP_Riders.pdf

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: BrightWorks redlines: order form + IP rider (output & training)

Hi Elena — thanks for the redlines and the memo. Appreciate how concrete this is. Short answers for now:

- Assignment carveout: we can't broadly assign model outputs; however, we can accept a narrow productization carveout that covers outputs that are literally copied into a BrightWorks product (e.g., content files, labelled assets) and provide an explicit, limited license for those cases.
- Training: we are not prepared to allow unrestricted training on customer data in the standard order form. We can offer a scoped feedback license that permits aggregated telemetry and non-identifiable usage for platform improvement, and we can negotiate a separate addendum if BrightWorks wants explicit retraining/fine-tuning rights for a fee and operational guardrails.
- Audit/telemetry: happy to provide quarterly telemetry summaries and a short audit window; need to sync with Security on format.

Looping Laura (AM) and Ben (Legal) to propose concrete language. I'm available tomorrow 10–11am PT or 3–4pm PT for a quick sync.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightWorks redlines: order form + IP rider (output & training)

Ben/Laura — forwarding BrightWorks' redlines. Key asks (copied from Elena's memo): assignment for outputs used in customer productization, no broad training license (scoped feedback only), opt-in telemetry and audit rights.

Ben: can you draft two short options we can share with BrightWorks tomorrow?

Option A (customer-friendly compromise):
- Redwood retains model weights and derivative models; BrightWorks gets an exclusive-like assignment only for outputs that are incorporated into BrightWorks' product artifacts (explicit list: UI copy exported as files, labeled datasets, code snippets incorporated into product repositories). For everything else, BrightWorks receives a perpetual, nonexclusive right to use outputs internally and commercially.
- Feedback license: allow aggregated telemetry + non-identifiable metrics for platform improvement; explicit opt-in required to share any telemetry derived from identifiable customer inputs.
- Retraining: separate commercial addendum required.

Option B (legal-preferred minimal change):
- Keep standard Redwood ownership (no assignment) but add a narrow operational warranty and an expedited support + discounted addendum process for customers who need retraining rights.

Laura: if BrightWorks pushes for assignment, we should coordinate on pricing/displacement risk (they're a mid-enterprise deal).

Tagging a doc: I attached 'redline_proposal_jb_v1.docx' with a lean set of edits. Please push back or reword.

—Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightWorks redlines: order form + IP rider (output & training)

Jordan/Laura — reviewed; attached is a tight proposal that I think is defensible and should be acceptable to BrightWorks with small edits. Highlights of proposed language (excerpt):

1) Outputs and Productization. "Customer Outputs" are defined as final output files or artifacts that are created solely from Customer Inputs and that Customer elects to export or persist outside the Redwood service (examples: exported UI copy files, labelled datasets exported as CSV/JSON, or customer-supplied training corpora enriched by model output). For such Customer Outputs, Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, reproduce, distribute, and create derivative works for Customer's internal or commercial purposes. This license does not transfer title to Redwood model weights, embeddings, or models.

2) Training / Feedback License. Customer may opt in to a "Scoped Feedback Program" to provide non-identifiable usage metrics and aggregated telemetry. Redwood will not use Customer Inputs or Customer Outputs for model retraining or fine-tuning unless Customer signs a separate Training Addendum that specifies scope, duration, pricing, and security controls.

3) Audit and Reporting. Redwood will provide quarterly aggregated telemetry reports for opted-in customers and allow one limited audit per 12 months to verify telemetry aggregation practices.

4) Narrow carveout for export-to-product. If Customer requires title assignment for exported outputs for a specific product line, we can consider a one-off assignment under a negotiated commercial fee and escrow terms for derivative models where necessary.

I kept the core Redwood position (we don't assign model weights) but give customers clear rights to outputs they export. This should address BrightWorks' productization ask while protecting our IP.

I'll attach the proposed redline (redline_proposal_jb_v1.docx). If you want, I can send directly to BrightWorks with a short cover note offering the two options (license + potential paid assignment path).

—Ben
Ben Carter | Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_proposal_jb_v1.docx

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightworks.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: BrightWorks redlines: order form + IP rider (output & training)

Ben/Jordan — thanks, this is helpful and much closer to what we need. Quick notes:

- The proposed "Customer Outputs" definition and the perpetual license look acceptable to our product team, provided we can carve out an example list in Schedule A for the initial go-live (we'll draft the examples but appreciate the structure).
- The Scoped Feedback Program language works, and the audit cadence is acceptable.
- On the one-off assignment: BrightWorks is open to a paid assignment for an initial product line (we'll propose commercial terms if Redwood is willing to proceed with escrow language for relevant model artifacts).

Can you please: (1) send the redline to us with the proposed Schedule A placeholder, and (2) share a short note on expected commercial bands for a one-off assignment (ballpark) so our procurement team can model it?

If you send this over today we can push it to our internal procurement review and, barring surprises, sign the order form next week.

Thanks,
Elena
--
Elena Morales | Sr. Counsel, BrightWorks
